title: SLO Operational Synchronization Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a deterministic, company-level process for synchronizing SLO status, error-budget consumption, and capacity actions across teams (Serving Runtime, SRE, Product, and Customer Success). It reduces decision latency during SLO degradations by codifying triggers, immediate mitigations, and a 3-hr to 72-hr follow-up cadence for longer remediation.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood inference services that expose customer-facing SLOs (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private control-plane endpoints). Does not supersede service-specific runbooks; it is the coordination layer used when cross-team activation is required.

Key goals:
- Align threshold definitions and ownership so oncall and product teams can act without back-and-forth.
- Provide a predictable capacity activation matrix tied to measured burn rates.
- Ensure incident review evidence is produced automatically and correlated to SLOs and capacity changes.

When to use this playbook
- Any alert that indicates accelerated SLO burn (see thresholds below).
- Capacity pressure events affecting multi-tenant model pools or cross-region routing.
- When product notices customer-impacting quality regressions traceable to model-serving capacity or configuration changes.

Preconditions
- Service must have a declared SLO and registered error budget in the SLO Ledger.
- Telemetry pipeline (slo-telemetry-prod) should be healthy; fallback: use synthetic canary results and request logs.
- Oncall contact lists and cross-team escalation channels (Slack: #sre-ops, #runtime-incident) configured.

Definitions and thresholds
- SLO types: latency_p99, latency_p95, availability_uptime_daily, correctness_regression_rate (where applicable).
- Error budget burn rate (30m window):
  - Green: < 1x expected burn
  - Elevated: 1x - 5x -> notify owner_team
  - Urgent: 5x - 15x -> immediate mitigation per matrix
  - Critical: > 15x or projected to exhaust budget in < 6 hours -> emergency capacity activation
- Burn % triggers (of monthly budget):
  - Advisory: 10% consumed -> product notification
  - Action: 25% consumed -> capacity hedging recommended
  - Escalate: 50% consumed -> mandatory intervention and SLO sync meeting
  - Emergency: 100% consumed -> broadfall procedures and customer comms

SLO synchronization procedure (step-by-step)
1) Detection (automatic):
   - slo-telemetry-prod emits a BurnRateAlert with tags {service, slo_id, region, tenant_shard}.
   - PagerDuty rule: Pager ID SLO-BURN-{service} triggers if burn >= Urgent for 2 consecutive 5m windows.
2) Immediate oncall actions (first 15 minutes):
   - Acknowledge the alert and post an incident thread to #sre-ops with summary: SLO, current burn, 1h projection, recently deployed revisions.
   - Run quick triage: check canary status, recent model rollouts, autoscaler events, and model KV cache eviction rates.
   - If evidence points to traffic spike: enable temporary priority-reshaping (see Capacity Activation Matrix) and throttle non-critical routes.
3) If no quick fix within 30 minutes -> SLO Sync huddle (virtual, 15 minutes):
   - Attendees: oncall SRE, runtime owner, product manager, customer success lead (if impacted tenant list exists).
   - Agenda: share evidence snapshot, decide immediate mitigations, determine whether to escalate to emergency capacity activation.
4) Follow-up (30m-3hr):
   - Implement agreed mitigations, document changes in the incident thread (who, what, why).
   - Monitor burn for recovery to Elevated/Green. If projection still suggests Critical within 6 hours, trigger escalation.
5) Escalation to incident execs (3hr+ or Critical):
   - Kick formal incident page, notify execs, coordinate customer notifications, and open post-incident action items (see Incident Review Linkage).

Capacity Activation Matrix (decision table)
| Condition | Action | Responsible | Target RTO |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Elevated (1x-5x) localized to shard | Apply route-priority reshaping, reduce batch size for noisy tenants | SRE + Runtime | 15m |
| Urgent (5x-15x), projected exhaust in 6-24h | Spin pre-provisioned warm GPUs (reserve pool), enable limited burst autoscale to Dedicated pools | Runtime infra + SRE | 30m - 1h |
| Critical (>15x) or multi-region spill | Cross-region failover, enable emergency extra capacity from elastic-reservoir, engage Sales/CS for customer comms | Platform SRE + Eng Leads | 1h - 3h |
| Model-serving regression (quality causing retries) | Re-route traffic to pinned stable model variants, rollback recent model shard rollout | Runtime + Applied ML | 15m - 1h |

Operational tooling and commands (examples)
- Inspect SLO burn via sloctl (internal CLI):
  - sloctl query --service inference-api --slo latency_p99 --window 30m
- Scale warm pool (example):
  - rictl capacity warmpool apply --name inference-warm-1 --gpus 8 --profile t4x16
- Temporarily restrict tenant routes: (policy-api):
  - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://policy.internal/v1/adjust -d '{"tenant_id":"TENANT-42","limit_qps":10}'
- Snapshot telemetry and attach to incident:
  - sloctl snapshot --service inference-api --range "-60m" --out /tmp/slo-snap.json && incident-cli attach --incident $INCIDENT_ID /tmp/slo-snap.json

Error budget reconciliation meeting (recommended cadence)
- When: mandatory when a service crosses 25% monthly consumption; weekly otherwise for high-risk services.
- Attendees: SLO steward, product manager, runtime owner, applied-ml rep, finance representative (cost impact).
- Goal: agree on corrective actions (optimize batching, change quantization profile, tenant throttles), cost vs risk tradeoffs, and schedule remediation within 7 calendar days.
- Output: updated action list with owners and acceptance criteria.

Incident review linkage and evidence standards
- For any SLO-related incident where error budget > 25% or customer impact:
  1) Attach SLO snapshots, request traces, and model rollout metadata to the incident (automated via incident-cli).
  2) Include capacity change diffs (who increased warmpool, when, and the impact).
  3) Annotate the postmortem with a clear remediation plan and a capacity safety-net implementation timeline.
- Evidence retention requirement: telemetry and attached artifacts retained for 365 days for all SLO incidents.

Operational playbook for recurring capacity debt
1) Identify services with repeated 25%+ monthly burns over 3 consecutive months.
2) Create a Capacity Debt ticket with template fields: root_cause, estimated_cost_to_fix, business_risk, rollback_plan, test_plan.
3) Prioritize into the quarterly reliability initiative backlog; include a remediation gate that requires pre-deploy load tests and SLO shadowing.

Ownership and escalation matrix
- Oncall SRE: initial triage and short-term mitigations.
- Runtime team: capacity provisioning, kernel/config changes, model pinned rollbacks.
- Product SLO steward: decision authority for risk tradeoffs and customer comms.
- Finance: approval for sustained extra contract capacity (> $50k/month).
- Escalation path: Oncall SRE -> Runtime Lead -> Head of SRE -> CTO (if > 24 hour customer-impacting outage).

Appendix: sample alert rule and playbook checklist
- Sample Prometheus-style alert (text):
  ALERT SLO_Burn_Urgent
  IF slo_burn_rate{service="inference-api",window="30m"} > 5
  FOR 5m
  LABELS {severity="urgent", team="sre"}
  ANNOTATIONS {summary="Inference API SLO burn >5x", runbook="/eng-sre/runbooks/slo-operational-synchronization-playbook-2026"}

- Playbook checklist (0-72h):
  - [ ] Acknowledge alert and capture snapshot (0-5m)
  - [ ] Quick triage: canary, recent deploys, autoscaler logs (0-15m)
  - [ ] Apply short-term mitigations (throttles, priority-reshaping) (0-30m)
  - [ ] Convene SLO Sync huddle (15m)
  - [ ] Spin warm pool / enable burst autoscale if required (30-90m)
  - [ ] Open Capacity Debt ticket if repeated burns (24-72h)
  - [ ] Publish post-incident action items and schedule remediation (72h)

Appendix B: sample incident postmortem template fields (for SLO incidents)
- Executive summary (1-2 sentences)
- Impact (tenants, requests lost, estimated revenue impact)
- Timeline of events and mitigation actions (timestamped with owners)
- Evidence artifacts (slo snapshot id, telemetry bundles, capacity change diffs)
- Root cause analysis and contributing factors
- Remediation plan with owners and due dates
- Lessons learned and prevention checklist

Notes and references
- This playbook is intentionally prescriptive for the first 3 hours, and consultative for remediation.
- Work with Product to ensure SLO definitions and the SLO Ledger metadata remain current.
- See related operational patterns: traffic-reshaper cookbook, warmpool orchestration guide, and the SLO observability fidelity spec.

Contact and ownership
